newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African bonds extended sharp gains made on Thursday as local and offshore buyers continued to pile into the market, dealers said.

And while gains were capped in the afternoon by pre-weekend profit-taking, traders were optimistic that the market would post renewed gains on Monday with some favouring a move below the 14 percent figure.
At 1415 GMT government's benchmark R150 bond was yielding 14.09 percent from an intraday best of 14.06 percent and 14.10 percent overnight.
"The initial target would be around 14 percent to 13.90 percent, technically speaking, but it's virtually impossible to call a bottom, one trader said.
Early Friday trade was marked by local profit-taking after aggressive offshore and local institutional buying pummeled bond yields to fresh 16 month lows on Friday.
Dealers said foreigners then took control of the market just before noon, triggering a mini panic buying spree which pushed yields lower to an intraday best of 14.06 percent.
"Sentiment is strong on the rand holding steady after the forex easing (this week), better U.S. Treasuries, improved liquidity in the money market and all this foreign interest," said the trader.
Others said the market had already discounted a two percentage point drop in local interest rates by year-end, which was also helping the bullish sentiment.
One trader noted that overseas banks had tended to come in after the official close, taking local banks out and forcing them to cover positions the following morning.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 156.16 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 732.6 million rand's worth on Wednesday.

On the forex market, the rand held to a tight 4.5230 to 4.5275 range for most of the day as local importer demand for dollars was balanced by offshore dollar selling -- sparked by interest in the bond market.
"The offshore guys were selling dollars to get rands to invest in the local bond market," a senior trader at a leading institution commented.

Most said there was a short-term stronger bias in the rand in the wake of a successful foreign exchange easing earlier this week but one or two expected importer demand at the lower levels to reign in the unit's gains.
Concerns about the continuing fall in the rand price of gold, which hit a 17-month low as the dollar bullion price slid to a 12-year low, had a minor impact on the currency on the day.
"The rand would maybe have traded as low as 4.5200 against the dollar on the day if not for the weaker gold price but nothing major," according to one trader.
He expected a tight 4.52 to 4.54 range next week.

In cross rate action, the unit continued under pressure against a rampant sterling. It was last trading at 7.6363/6459 from 7.6112/6208 overnight. It was quoted little changed at 0.3872/3876 marks from 0.3864/3868 ovenight and at 25.0806/1193 yen from 25.0768/1155 yen previously.

On the money market, three-month NCDs fell to between 15.65 to 15.70 percent offered from between 14.75 and 14.80 percent on Thursday, while the 90-day BA rate was also slightly lower at between 15.25 and 15.10 percent from 15.15 to 15.35 percent.
The Reserve Bank quoted the money market shortage lower at 5.250 billion rand on Thursday from 5.379 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
